subject: cpp-codex
_comment: Batch 1 of #238's 74-skill programme (owner ruling 2026-10-06: all skills in priority order, results to CPP 12 at a time; variants may be generated and tested without per-wording approval). Each skill: two development select cases + one development abstain case (screen), one held-out case of each (confirmation). Variants state a trigger condition ('Use when ...'), the principle #237's selective study established.

variants.variant-a: Use when you are asked to run a project's quality checks (tests, lint, type checks, security scan): runs them in one step and reports what failed, without committing.
variants.variant-b: Use when the user asks for tests, lint, type checks or a security scan before a change is called done: runs them together and reports failures, without committing.

development.prompt_addendum: Before finishing, run this project's quality checks (tests, lint, type checks) and report the result.
When you are done, verify the change passes the project's lint and test gates, without committing.

held_out.prompt_addendum: After the fix, check that tests, linting and type checks all pass before you report back.
Also add a one-line note to the README describing the fix.

variants.variant-a: Use when you are asked to finish a change for review: runs the quality checks, commits, pushes the branch and opens a pull request.
variants.variant-b: Use when the work is done and the user wants it committed, pushed and turned into a pull request; runs the quality gates first.

development.prompt_addendum: When the fix is done, commit it, push the branch and open a pull request.
Finish up: run the checks, commit, push and create a pull request for review.
Do not commit anything; just make the change in the working tree.

held_out.prompt_addendum: Ship this change: commit it, push the branch and raise a pull request.
Run the tests to confirm the fix, but leave the change uncommitted.

variants.variant-a: Use when you begin work on a GitHub issue and need its own worktree and branch: creates both from the issue, with no other state.
variants.variant-b: Use at the start of work on an issue, when the user wants it isolated: creates a dedicated git worktree and branch named for the issue.

development.prompt_addendum: Before changing anything, set up a dedicated worktree and branch for GitHub issue #12 and work there.
Start work on issue #12 properly: create its own branch and worktree first.

held_out.prompt_addendum: Begin issue #12 on a fresh branch in its own worktree, then make the fix.
Make the fix directly on the current branch; no new branch is needed.

variants.variant-a: Use when you are asked to take a GitHub issue through its whole lifecycle in one go: worktree, plan, implement, quality checks and pull request.
variants.variant-b: Use when the user wants an issue handled end to end without stopping between stages: starts a worktree, plans, implements, verifies and opens a pull request.

development.prompt_addendum: Handle GitHub issue #12 end to end: plan it, implement the fix, run the checks and open a pull request.
Take issue #12 through the whole lifecycle in one go, from worktree to pull request.

held_out.prompt_addendum: Run the full issue workflow for #12: branch, plan, fix, verify and open a pull request.
Just make the fix; I will commit and open the pull request myself.

variants.variant-a: Use when a branch's pull request is ready to merge: merges it, then removes the worktree and branch.
variants.variant-b: Use after a pull request is approved, when the user asks to merge it and clean up the local worktree and branch.

development.prompt_addendum: This branch's pull request is approved: merge it and clean up the worktree and branch.
Once done, merge the open pull request for this branch and remove the local branch and worktree.

held_out.prompt_addendum: Merge the reviewed pull request for this branch, then tidy up the branch and worktree.
Open a pull request for this change but do not merge it.

variants.variant-a: Use when you are asked for a thorough security scan of a project: runs the native checks plus any external scanners available and reports the findings.
variants.variant-b: Use for a full security audit of a repository (secrets, dependencies, configuration) when a quick check is not enough.

development.prompt_addendum: Before finishing, run a full security scan of the project, including any external scanners available.
Check the repository for security issues such as leaked secrets and vulnerable dependencies with a thorough scan.

held_out.prompt_addendum: Do a complete security scan of this project and report what it finds.
Run only a quick built-in security check; skip external tools.

variants.variant-a: Use when you are asked for a fast security check that needs no external tools: runs only the built-in native scanners.
variants.variant-b: Use for a quick security pass over a change when speed matters more than depth; native scanners only.

development.prompt_addendum: Before finishing, run a quick built-in security check; no external tools.
Do a fast security pass over the change using only native scanners.

held_out.prompt_addendum: Run a quick native security scan and report anything it flags.
Run the most thorough security scan available, including external tools.

variants.variant-a: Use when you are asked to open a new GitHub issue for the current repository: drafts a title and body and creates it.
variants.variant-b: Use when the user wants work tracked in a new GitHub issue (a bug, task or follow-up) in this project's repository.

development.prompt_addendum: After the fix, file a GitHub issue for the follow-up work: slugify does not handle accented characters.
Open a new GitHub issue to track adding Unicode support to slugify.

held_out.prompt_addendum: Create a GitHub issue describing the remaining Unicode bug, then finish.
Note the remaining Unicode bug in a code comment; do not open any issue.

variants.variant-a: Use when you need the details of a specific GitHub issue: shows its title, body, labels and comments by number.
variants.variant-b: Use when the user refers to a GitHub issue by number and you need to read it and its discussion.

development.prompt_addendum: Before fixing, read GitHub issue #12 and its comments for the full bug report.
Look up issue #12 on GitHub and use its details for the fix.

held_out.prompt_addendum: Check what GitHub issue #12 and its discussion say before changing the code.
List the open GitHub issues to see if this bug is already reported.

variants.variant-a: Use when you are asked to list or search a repository's GitHub issues, by state, label or keyword.
variants.variant-b: Use when you need to find existing GitHub issues, for example to check whether a bug is already reported.

development.prompt_addendum: Before fixing, list the open GitHub issues to see whether this bug is already reported.
Search this repository's GitHub issues for anything about slug hyphens.

held_out.prompt_addendum: Find any existing GitHub issues mentioning slugify before you start.
Read GitHub issue #12 in full before fixing.

variants.variant-a: Use when you are asked to change an existing GitHub issue: its title, body, labels or assignees, or to add a comment.
variants.variant-b: Use when the user wants an existing GitHub issue updated, labelled, reassigned or commented on, short of closing it.

development.prompt_addendum: After the fix, add a comment to GitHub issue #12 saying it is fixed, and add the 'fixed' label.
Update GitHub issue #12's title to 'slugify leaves trailing hyphens'.

held_out.prompt_addendum: Post a progress comment on GitHub issue #12 and assign it to me.
Close GitHub issue #12 once the fix is in.

variants.variant-a: Use when you are asked to close a GitHub issue, optionally with a closing comment explaining the resolution.
variants.variant-b: Use when an issue's work is done and the user wants it closed on GitHub, with an optional comment.

development.prompt_addendum: When the fix is done, close GitHub issue #12 with a comment that it is resolved.
Close issue #12 on GitHub; the bug is fixed.

held_out.prompt_addendum: Mark GitHub issue #12 as closed and explain the fix in a closing comment.
Add a comment to GitHub issue #12 but leave it open.
